checks.claim: Gas dissolved in magma comes out as bubbles as the magma rises, and their expansion drives explosive eruptions
checks.why: NPS and the USGS soda bottle activity: falling pressure lets dissolved gas form bubbles whose expansion blasts magma out.

checks.claim: Stratovolcanoes are built of alternating layers of lava flows and ash
checks.why: USGS: repeated eruptions from one vent build overlapping layers of lava and ash, a composite volcano or stratovolcano.

checks.claim: Lava that meets water cools quickly into rock, often with bursts of steam
checks.why: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory: lava entering water is chilled on contact, shatters into glassy rock and sends up steam plumes.
